creative_rules.synthesis_source: CREATIVE_GAP_ANALYSIS.md; ANALYZER_V3_SPEC.md (CROSS-PRODUCT LEARNING ARCHITECTURE section); PROJECT_STATUS.md session 25

permanent_rules.title: Open on a real hand/person already using the product, not a static product render.
Avoid marketplace/catalog-style product presentation; use native real-world product demonstration instead.
permanent_rules.revised_from: Original narrow Rule 2 wording ('never show an AliExpress screenshot') was MODIFIED by Product 008, which shows glossy static CGI/catalog presentation without a literal marketplace screenshot. The broader revised wording above earned permanent status on its own 16/16 vs. 0/20 evidence.

evidence.notes: Products 002/003/007: literal AliExpress/marketplace screenshots. Product 008: glossy static CGI/catalog presentation without literal marketplace UI -- same underlying defect, different mechanism.

permanent_rules.title: Show the product's actual mechanism/action/use rather than merely displaying the product.
permanent_rules.sharpest_example: Product 008: the core '360-degree rotation' benefit is represented by a static arrow graphic instead of actual rotation footage.

modified_rules.title: Include meaningful creative progression beyond a flat/basic demo.
examples: another meaningful progression rather than a flat uninterrupted presentation

combined_layer_3_5_7_diagnosis.layer_3_what: Our videos open with static/catalog-style product presentation.
combined_layer_3_5_7_diagnosis.layer_7_when: Among the 12 statistically usable variants (>=10 views), 2-second retention is approximately 0.25-0.45 and none are STRONG.
combined_layer_3_5_7_diagnosis.layer_5_how: 20/20 QA-verified successful competitor videos use real human/product interaction and demonstrate the real mechanism instead of our static/catalog presentation.

have: direct evidence about our own retention (Layer 7)
do_not_have: causal proof that changing the creative rules will improve retention
forbidden_claims: competitors retain viewers better at 2 seconds

data_quality_findings.finding: Apparent STRONG retention results in the portfolio are not reliable wins -- both are driven by tiny sample size, not real creative success.
data_quality_findings.usable_variant_outcomes: all WEAK or MARGINAL, none STRONG

status_for_creative_pipeline.note: The 3 permanent rules are strong cross-product recommendations based on repeated correlation, NOT causally proven performance improvements. They are adopted as REQUIREMENTS for the next creative test, not as confirmed wins.
status_for_creative_pipeline.rule_4_status: NOT permanent -- must not be applied as a hard requirement by the creative pipeline yet.

next_causal_test.purpose: The next creative should function as a causal test of the 3 permanent rules.
next_causal_test.comparison_goal: Measured retention/performance on the NEW pattern vs. historical OLD-pattern variants determines whether the correlations translate into real improvement.

product_009_brief.lead_hook_reason: Highest average views across CONFIRMED runs (229.5 vs 158.0/157.5/116.0) and, for the first time, the most reliable 2-second retention average (42.8%) once Problem/Solution's tiny-sample outlier (003C, 1 view) is excluded -- Problem/Solution has the higher raw win count (2/4 vs 1/4) but that edge does not hold up once retention data is factored in.
product_009_brief.first_frame_requirement: standard approach -- 2s retention is WEAK-to-MARGINAL but not CRITICAL on any statistically meaningful variant, meaning the hook itself is not the primary problem
product_009_brief.pacing_adjustment: shorten and tighten the mid-video (5-13s) segments -- average watch time is POOR (<25% of the 15s runtime) on 13 of 16 variants, including several high-view variants; viewers consistently leave well before the video ends regardless of hook type
product_009_brief.cta_adjustment: no data yet -- cta_code_comments has never been collected for any product; this is now the top data-quality gap
product_009_brief.storyboard_notes: consider testing a shorter/faster-paced middle section as an explicit experiment, given how consistent the watch-time drop-off is across every hook type and product tested so far. This is the first analysis run backed by complete saves/shares/watch-time/retention data -- prior PROCEED decisions (including 2026-07-01's) were built on incomplete data per PROJECT_STATUS.md.
